prerequisites: A complete vision as possible of the technical disciplines taught in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Ability for the prevention of occupational risks and protection of the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Understand the legal and ethical requirements and implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social and ethical conditions to be considered in them.

Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all tasks necessary to carry it out, and carry out progress control and supervision of the work to be done in a project, keeping in mind the initial planning.
Clearly explain and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents that allow its contracting and execution.
Know the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as elaborate and improve a work method.

syllabus_topics: Topic 6: Regulatory Scope and Project Processing.
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (problem solving and case studies)
Computer lab practices (application of planning, budgeting, graphic and document management tools)

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory Practices (EV-3). Practical skills. (Exercises and Lab Exam)

assessment_rules: To pass in the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a minimum score of 5 out of 10 in each of the three parts (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3). If these minimums are reached, the final grade will be calculated as: Note = 0.4 * EV-1 + 0.35 * EV-2 + 0.25 * EV-3. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated note and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, grades above 5 in any part can be saved, or the student can re-take the exam for that part. For differentiated evaluation, attendance to practices is not mandatory; exercises will count for 25% and the lab exam for 75% in EV-3 for the ordinary call, while for the extraordinary call, EV-3 will be solely the lab exam grade.
